doc.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015

title: Wycliffe Gordon and how he came to lead the Jazz Cruise big band
summary: Hearing Wycliffe Gordon leads to the Jazz Cruise and how Ken Peplowski handed him the all-star big band.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Great. Here’s a guy who’s I think somewhat younger than you.

Wycliffe [Gordon]? Yeah. That one spot and you could tell it’s him. Yeah he’s another guy with just a freaky set of chops. I mean technically he can go anywhere. And a lot of energy and a lot of air. Yeah. I’ve been working with him over the last six years now I guess. Every year in January I do this thing called the Jazz Cruise, which is an entire giant cruise ship dedicated entirely to jazz. No other entertainment on the boat. No Broadway shows, no silly whatever — someone making balloon animals. It’s all jazz and they bring out all these great players. And I first did it in 2009 and they used to always bring a big band on in addition to all these collections of guys playing in small groups all over the ship. And then in 2009 they decided let’s try putting all these guys together for the big band, to have like an all-star big band. And I was just a sideman at the time. Ken Peplowski, a clarinet player, was leading the band. And after that year he invited me back and he said, “you know what? Bring some charts. And this was getting to be a little too much for me.” Because he was doing everything. He was setting up all the entertainment, he was playing, he was running the big band. He said, “let’s split off — you take a couple of nights and I’ll take a couple of nights.” And then after we did that year he said, “you know what? It’s yours. I’d rather just play.” And so I’ve been leading that band since then. And the first couple of years Wycliffe did it. But he’s always on the ship. But he’s not always in the big band. But what a fantastic talent. Really great guy too.
